title: Access, Change & Procurement Playbook — Compact Guide
intro:
Purpose
  This compact playbook consolidates Redwood Inference company-wide policies and operational patterns for access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, travel expense handling, and the canonical templates teams should reuse. It is designed for day-to-day reference by engineering, product, security, people-ops, and finance teams. Use this as an operational checklist and a set of enforced thresholds; it links to detailed procedures where required.
overview:
Scope
  - Applies to all full-time employees (FTEs), contractors, and vendors with company accounts or physical access.
  - Covers lifecycle from request -> approval -> provisioning -> review for access; request -> approval -> rollout -> post-change verification for changes; request -> approval -> purchase -> invoice for procurement; and vendor security/contract checks before onboarding.
  - Exceptions must follow the Risk & Exceptions workflow (security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions) and be timeboxed.
key-contacts:
Owners and escalation
  - Policy owner: Finance & Legal (owner_team)
  - Day-to-day steward: Security (access operations)
  - Procurement contact: Procurement Manager (procurement@redwood.ai)
  - Emergency on-call: Eng SRE rotation (see eng-sre/oncall-rotations)
access-permissions:
Access lifecycle summary
  1) Request: Use the central Access Request form (internal link: /forms/access-request). Always include justification and data classification of resources requested.
  2) Approval matrix: Requests require one of the following approvers depending on resource tier:
     - Tier 1 (public docs, non-sensitive tools): Team lead or manager. SLA: 48 business hours.
     - Tier 2 (internal systems, non-production infra): Product/Engineering manager + Security approval. SLA: 72 business hours.
     - Tier 3 (production systems, customer data, KMS/HSM, admin roles): Manager + Security review + Finance if billing impact. SLA: 5 business days.
  3) Provisioning: Automated where possible (IAM flows). Manual steps must be tracked in the ticket. Record the provisioning ticket ID in the access request.
  4) Review & recertification: Quarterly recertification for Tier 3 and semi-annual for Tier 2. All teams run a role-review runbook before offboarding events.
  5) Emergency access: Temporary elevated access issued via Break-Glass process. Emergency access screenshots, reason, and postmortem must be attached to the original request within 48 hours.

  Access controls & thresholds (table)
  | Resource class | Example services | Default TTL | Approval required |
  |---|---|---:|---|
  | Tier 1 (Low) | Public docs, marketing tools | 90 days | Team lead |
  | Tier 2 (Moderate) | Staging clusters, internal dashboards | 30 days | Manager + Security |
  | Tier 3 (High) | Production GPU clusters, KMS, customer data | 7 days (renew) | Manager + Security + Finance |
change-management:
Change policy at-a-glance
  - All changes that affect production paths, security posture, or billing above $10k/month must enter the Change Review workflow.
  - Types of changes:
    a) Standard changes: Pre-approved and recurring (e.g., routine infra patching). Require CAB notification only.
    b) Normal changes: Require pre-approval, rollout plan, backout plan, and post-change verification.
    c) Emergency changes: Bypass normal CAB timelines with documented justification and a post-implementation review within 72 hours.

  Change process (numbered)
  1. Create change ticket in the Change queue with classification, impact analysis, rollback plan, owner, and proposed window.
  2. Peer review & security review: Security approves if any sensitive data, network, or IAM changes are included.
  3. CAB review: Weekly CAB meets for Normal changes. Approvals logged in the ticket.
  4. Runbook execution: Follow the runbook for the service, including pre-checks and canary rollout (10% traffic for 30 minutes typical).
  5. Verification & close: Post-change verification checklist completed and attached to the ticket. Record any incidents in oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems.
data-management:
Data classification
  - PUBLIC: Intended for public disclosure. No special handling.
  - INTERNAL: Company operational data. Access controlled but not regulated.
  - CONFIDENTIAL: Customer data, PII, financials. Strong access controls and encryption required.
  - RESTRICTED: Regulated data (e.g., health, payment card). Requires compliance controls and restricted hosting.

  Handling rules (bullets)
  - All CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED data must be encrypted at rest and in transit using company-approved KMS.
  - Data minimization: Only store fields required for the purpose. Retention schedules must be applied per the Data Retention matrix.
  - Data export: Exports of CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data require Security + Legal approval and an approved export ticket.
procurement-and-expenses:
Purchasing thresholds & approval
  - Low-touch purchases (< $2,500): Team budget owner approval. Use corporate card or expense report.
  - Mid-tier purchases ($2,500 - $50,000): Manager + Procurement approval and standard PO.
  - High-value purchases (> $50,000): Procurement + Finance + Legal. Contract review required.

  Procurement process (steps)
  1. Initiate PR (Purchase Request) with justification, GL code, and vendor details.
  2. Procurement evaluates vendor terms, compliance evidence, and price competitiveness.
  3. Finance validates budget availability and issues PO.
  4. Receipt and invoice matching: AP validates and follows 3-way match.

  Expense policy highlights
  - Travel per diem: see travel policy summary below. Personal expenses are non-reimbursable.
  - Receipts required for all expenses > $25. Use the Expense system with proper GL coding.
vendor-management:
Onboarding checklist
  - Vendor intake form completed with business case and data access requirements.
  - Security questionnaire: Vendor must complete the security questionnaire if they process CONFIDENTIAL or RESTRICTED data.
  - Contract & SOW: Legal negotiates terms, includes data protection addenda and breach notification timelines.
  - Access controls: Least-privilege IAM accounts, dedicated service accounts, and timeboxed credentials where possible.

  Vendor risk thresholds
  - Low: SaaS without data access. Approval: Procurement.
  - Medium: SaaS with internal data access. Approval: Procurement + Security.
  - High: Processes CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data or has system access. Approval: Procurement + Security + Legal + Exec sponsor.
travel-and-expenses:
Travel guidelines
  - Booking: Use approved travel portal. Economy or equivalent for domestic travel; premium economy for flights over 6 hours with manager approval.
  - Pre-approval: All travel above $1,000 requires manager pre-approval.
  - Per diem: Meals up to $75/day; incidentals up to $25/day. Exceptions require manager approval.

  Expense submission timeline
  - Submit within 30 days of expense. Late submissions may be denied without manager exception.
canonical-templates:
Reusable templates
  - Access request subject: [Access Request] <Resource> — <Justification>
  - Change ticket name: [Change][<Service>] <Short summary> — rollout <date>
  - Purchase request template (CSV fields): requester, vendor, justification, gl_code, cost_estimate, contract_required (yes/no)

  Sample Access Request (copyable)
  -------------------------------
  Title: [Access Request] S3 project-buckets — analytics team
  Requested by: <name>
  Resource: s3://redwood-analytics/project-buckets
  Tier: Tier 2
  Justification: Required for daily ETL runs producing product analytics. No PII expected; storing aggregated metrics.
  Duration: 90 days
  Approvers: Team lead; Security if escalated

  Sample Change Checklist (to attach to ticket)
  - Pre-change snapshot/backups taken: yes/no
  - Rollout window: HH:MM UTC
  - Canary % and duration: 10% for 30m
  - Rollback plan: exact steps + owner
  - Post-change verification metric(s): error-rate <= 0.5%, latency within SLO
escalation-and-exceptions:
Exceptions
  - Requestors may ask for exceptions using the Risk & Exceptions form. Exceptions must include duration, compensating controls, owner, and sunset date.

  Escalation ladder (short)
  1. Team lead
  2. Service owner
  3. Security / Procurement
  4. Head of Finance/Legal (for vendor/contract issues)
